reviewCriteria: Keep each domain fact, decision, and capability under one authoritative owner and operation.
Keep provider-specific SDK and wire details inside the owning adapter; shared contracts stay provider-neutral and runtime-validated.
Trace only surfaces required by the current request or product contract through routing, registration, inventory, and dependency injection; do not add surfaces for parity or symmetry.
Use deterministic logic for hard invariants and fail explicitly when a core AI capability is unavailable.
Fix the failure class at its owning layer rather than suppressing one symptom; the fix covers every instance of the reported failure class within the change scope and reports instances outside it.
Prefer reuse, then deletion, then addition; new abstraction needs a real ownership boundary or stable domain concept.
Reject unrelated refactors, speculative flags, duplicated truth, and gate bypasses.
Choose the smallest sufficient solution; a heavier permanent mechanism needs current evidence naming what the smaller option cannot cover and its ongoing cost.
Support claims with current evidence at the claimed boundary; static checks and mocks do not prove live behavior.
Derive relevant success, rejection, failure and boundary cases from the changed contract and reachable risks.
Trace test setup, execution and assertions: valid behavior must pass; the original defect or a representative contract violation must fail.
Check actual execution and outcomes; skipped or empty runs, swallowed errors and fallback cannot prove required behavior.
Report concrete verification gaps independently of product defects; name the requirement or risk, source evidence and needed check.
State inspected, executed and unverified scope; green checks or no findings do not prove completeness.
Reject new escape hatches, skipped checks, focused tests, secret leaks, merge markers, and unexplained threshold bypasses.
Prefer readable names, explicit boundary errors, validated external input, and high-cohesion ownership.
Treat style as maintainability evidence, not a substitute for behavioral correctness.
Localhost, child processes, SDK callbacks, tool output, and machine-generated content are not trusted merely because they are local or structured.
Validate the actual untrusted data or authority before privileged state or side effects; authenticate identity and authorize the requested action separately.
Preserve native permission authority, fail closed on missing or malformed values, and never expose secrets in output.
Add only controls matched to an actual boundary and threat, such as safe paths, argument arrays, parameterized queries, origin checks, or size limits.
A loop needs an evaluable target, signal, cap, and stop condition before it starts.
Each iteration stays on one hypothesis and records evidence.
Stop on success, cap, repeated blocker, or stalled signal; token and external-service cost need a stronger stopping rule.
Review the full authorized change range and keep commits focused on one logical change.
Do not weaken gates, stage unrelated work, or perform commit, push, PR, merge, or release actions without authorization.
Verification must cover the changed failure mode and delivery summaries must match the actual diff.

Proceed on reversible, in-scope, verifiable work; ask before outward-facing actions, scope expansion, or when two plausible interpretations would change the target, behavior, or external effect and current evidence cannot resolve intent.

Count only a completed corrective action based on a stated root-cause hypothesis and followed by relevant verification as a fix attempt; inspection and reruns without a corrective action do not count, nor do tool, sandbox, or permission failures that prevent the action from completing or verification from running.

After two attempts under one hypothesis leave the same verification blocked by the same failure class, return to diagnosis; cosmetic output changes do not reset the count, but a different failure class or new evidence-backed hypothesis does.
Ask only when continuing requires user authority, a scope decision, or external state change; never weaken a test, assertion, type, or lint rule to pass.
A successful-looking fix without a causal explanation is not verified.

Record only repo-scoped decisions with lasting architectural or process consequences, using the repository's existing convention; leave the shortest useful handoff in an existing location only for work another session must continue.
Do not duplicate facts already owned by code or git history, create a new record unless the repository or user requires it, or persist memory without host policy and user authority.
Supersede conflicting records and verify recalled state before acting on it.
Verify single authoritative truth, no dead code, and complete wiring only to surfaces required by the current request or product contract.
Reject symptom patches, duplicated authority, provider leakage, and unsafe permission bypasses.
Require live evidence for provider, authentication, permission, process, platform, and deployment claims.
Prefer deterministic ownership of known formats and safety invariants; isolate optional AI failure.
Support product defects with a reachable failure path; support verification gaps with an explicit requirement or concrete risk and evidence of missing or ineffective checks.
